frames.narration: The search team's app sends a streaming chat request for the logical model 'assistant-large', with its team key. The prompt is 1,800 tokens and the caller allows at most 500 tokens of output. The gateway authenticates the key and maps it to the search team.
Before anything runs, the gateway reserves 1,800 + 500 = 2,300 tokens from the team's per-minute bucket. The bucket held 31,000, so 28,700 remain and the request is allowed.

The gateway looks up the prefix cache by a hash of the first blocks of the prompt. The first 1,200 tokens, the system prompt, are already cached on GPU replica 2, so only 600 tokens need processing. The answer cache has no match for this question.

The router picks the company GPU pool because it is healthy and already paid for, and prefers replica 2 for its cached prefix. The provider stays as the fallback. The request joins the admission queue as interactive traffic: 3 requests wait, below the limit of 16, so it is admitted.
A slot frees up and the request starts. Replica 2 processes the 600 new tokens and produces the first token 420 ms after the request arrived. That is the time to first token, and it is recorded.
Tokens flow back as they are produced. The gateway passes each one to the app as a server-sent event, so the user watches the answer appear without waiting for the end.

After 180 tokens the user closes the tab. The gateway sees the closed connection and cancels the request on the replica, which frees its slot at once. The call used 1,800 + 180 = 1,980 tokens, so 320 of the reservation go back to the bucket and 29,020 remain.

One usage event is written for the call: team search, model assistant-large, 600 uncached and 1,200 cached input tokens, 180 output tokens, outcome cancelled. At the large model's prices this costs about $0.0049, charged to the search team.
